name: Skeleton
purpose: Render a pulsing placeholder shape in place of content that hasn't finished loading, preserving the layout the real content will fill.
intent: Reduce perceived load time and layout shift, distinct from Spinner (no implied layout) and ProgressBar (measurable progress).

apiAdaptationNotes: Figma instances freely override width, height, and corner radius per usage rather than exposing them as named variants - the component formalizes the corner-radius axis as a `shape` prop (`rectangle` | `circle`, following Icon Tile's shape-prop convention) and leaves width/height to forwarded `style`/`className`, matching ProgressBar's existing convention for per-usage sizing.

Figma's prototype has an AFTER_TIMEOUT reaction smart-animating between the `default` and `subtle` variants every 1.5s as a way to preview a pulse effect inside Figma - the component instead implements the pulse as a self-contained CSS opacity animation on a single variant, so it animates on its own regardless of which `appearance` is selected.

antiPatterns: indeterminate waits with no known final layout (use Spinner)
visible loading copy next to a labelled Skeleton

anatomy.description: Sized, colored, rounded placeholder shape that pulses on an infinite loop.
Rendered only when the `label` prop is set; announces the loading state to assistive technology.

appearance.description: Visual weight of the placeholder fill.

shape.description: Corner treatment - circle is fully round, for avatar-shaped placeholders.

label.description: Accessible loading announcement. When set, renders role=status/aria-live=polite instead of aria-hidden.

default.purpose: A more visible placeholder fill for full-page loading states.

subtle.purpose: A lighter placeholder fill for dense layouts (the default).

rectangle.purpose: Standard small corner radius for text lines, cards, and blocks.

circle.purpose: Fully round radius for avatar-shaped placeholders.

sizing.override: Forwarded style/className on the root div - no dedicated width/height props.

labelled.whenSet: role=status, aria-live=polite, visually-hidden announcement of the label text

requirements: Set label only when no adjacent context already conveys that the region is loading.
Disable the pulse animation under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

behaviorRules: Do not add hover, press, active, or disabled states.
Default appearance is subtle, default shape is rectangle.
Apply data-appearance and data-shape equal to the selected values.
Pulse continuously via CSS animation regardless of which appearance is selected.
Forward all native div attributes (including style and a ref) via ...rest.
compositionRules: Skeleton has no children slot - compose multiple Skeletons to sketch a loading layout.
Use Spinner instead if the final layout/shape is unknown.
Use ProgressBar instead when progress is measurable.
Pair shape=circle with an equal inlineSize/blockSize in style for a true circle.
contentRules: No text content of its own outside the visually-hidden label.
themeRules: Must work in light and dark themes.
All fill colors use semantic/component CSS variables that already resolve per-theme.
implementationNotes: Use React.memo and React.forwardRef for the exported component.
No hardcoded colors, spacing, radius, or motion timing when tokens exist.

Component color tokens --component-skeleton-color-default and --component-skeleton-color-subtle (both aliasing brand-taupe alpha primitives after the taupe token migration; the earlier semantic color-skeleton-default was removed when Figma dropped it), primitive duration-loop-slow (1500ms), and semantic motion pulse-loop - all read directly off Figma's boundVariables/reactions, not guessed.
No dedicated width/height props - forwarded style/className cover arbitrary per-usage sizing, matching ProgressBar's existing convention.
do: Size each Skeleton to match the content it's replacing.
Compose multiple Skeletons to sketch a full loading layout.
Pass label when a Skeleton is the sole loading indicator.
dont: Do not use for an indeterminate wait with no known layout.
Do not use for measurable/quantified progress.
Do not add visible loading copy next to a labelled Skeleton.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders a non-interactive div by default.
Supports all SkeletonAppearance and SkeletonShape values.
Applies data-appearance and data-shape for the selected values.
label unset (default) renders aria-hidden with no role.
label set renders role=status, aria-live=polite, and a visually-hidden announcement.
Supports className and forwards native div attributes (including style) via ...rest.
Forwards a ref to the root element.
Uses tokenized color, radius, sizing, and motion for both appearances and shapes.
Pulse animation is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
Storybook includes Playground, Variants, and Composition.
Tests cover defaults, each prop, className, ref forwarding, style sizing, accessibility, and token usage.
knownLimitations: No dedicated width/height props - callers must use style/className for sizing.
No multi-line text preset - compose multiple Skeletons for a paragraph.
futureEnhancements: A text shape preset rendering multiple lines of varying width in one component, if a recurring multi-line pattern emerges across products
